title: gap_scanner.py's after-hours shortlist: does it predict next-day performance?

tables.name: After-hours gap buckets: real vs random control, TRAIN + VAL

notes: gap_scanner.py has run track-only since 2026-07-10 with no validation of its own premise -- its docstring explicitly says it needs the same validation-before-trust discipline as intraday_scanner.py, the sibling scanner that WAS validated and retired for no edge. This is that check for the after-hours half (gap_universe_calibration.py already answered the pre-market half: no edge outside the existing top-50 accumulation shortlist). Reuses gap_scanner's own real historical shortlist output via gap_scan.json's git history in the public dashboard repo (cloned fresh at runtime, read-only), rather than re-fetching full-universe historical intraday data from scratch. Tests BOTH continuation and mean-reversion directions, not just continuation -- a fade pattern is just as real/actionable a finding as a momentum one.

conclusion.summary: Correlation TRAIN=-0.10524176597338916, VAL=-0.39586569947630096 (95% CI excludes zero on both, same sign: False). Continuation pattern (HIGH beats LOW) on both splits: False. Mean-reversion pattern (LOW beats HIGH) on both splits: True. HIGH-gap bucket vs its own random-shuffle control -- beats it: False, underperforms it: False. No real edge detected in gap_scanner after-hours data as currently scoped.
